items.title: The 8:30: The stories driving markets September 24
items.summary: Yahoo Finance's Julie Hyman, Jake Conley, and Pras Subramanian break down the biggest market and business stories driving the day's conversation. From the latest moves in stocks and bonds to key corporate news and economic developments, the 8:30 panel delivers the essential headlines and market context you need to start your day informed.

items.title: Looking for consumer and investor sentiment trends? Turn to social media.
items.summary: Jessica Inskip, StockBrokers.com director of Investor Research, explains to the Market Hang panel how social media algorithms are great for gauging investor sentiment and consumer demand.

items.title: A New Brand Of Inflation Slams This Smartphone Segment
items.summary: Still healing from sticker shock after Apple's latest launch? You may want to look away. A variation on the force driving up even the price of year-old iPhones — to say nothing of $3,000-plus models — is chomping away at budget phones. items.title: Klarna Falls 3% as Selling Persists Weeks After Its Guidance Cut; Affirm Advances 2%
items.summary: Klarna keeps sliding weeks after a guidance cut rattled investors, while Affirm moves in the opposite direction as traders rally around its AI underwriting push. The widening gap between two of fintech's biggest names raises a pointed question about which side of this trade holds up.

items.title: Chip Stocks Retreat. Qualcomm Secures Apple Licensing Deal.
items.summary: Chip stocks fell along with the broader market on Thursday as the U.S. and China held trade talks in Washington, D.C.

items.title: Welcome to the age of listening devices
items.summary: Devices that can listen and record us are becoming more popular, raising privacy concerns.

items.title: Qualcomm Renews Global Apple Patent License — Extends Key Licensing Relationship Into 2027
items.summary: The renewal with Apple comes as Qualcomm expands its latest Snapdragon lineup around agentic AI and lands its new Reality Elite processor in Meta’s upcoming VR glasses.

items.title: Qualcomm or Cisco: One Dividend Will Outpace the Other From Here
items.summary: Qualcomm and Cisco both raise their dividends every year and both are racing into AI infrastructure, but their capital allocation priorities point in completely different directions for a retiree who needs the income to be reliable.
